title: Book Two · Chapter 86: The Last Two Steps
story:
Spring returns. At school, the children have a short running game in the clear part of the yard. It is an ordinary afternoon activity. There are no prizes. Nobody makes a list of the best runners.

Ronan stands beside Leo. Jun waits at the far end with two other children. They mark the finish with chalk. The teacher watches them.

“Ready?” Leo asks.

Ronan nods. He bends his knees a little. When the teacher calls, they run.

For the first half, Leo is ahead. Ronan sees his elbow just in front. He wants to look at Leo's face. But he still needs to reach the line. He keeps his eyes on it and moves his arms.

The last two steps feel very long. Ronan reaches the line with Leo beside him. Jun points at Ronan.

“Just first.”

Ronan stops beyond the line and turns. His breath comes fast. He lifts one fist. Then he lifts both.

“Again,” Leo says.

“After I breathe.”

Leo bends with his hands on his knees. He is breathing hard too. Jun waits for them to rest. Then he takes his own turn.

Ronan watches Jun race another child. Jun loses by a large step. He walks back with a very serious face.

“I let him use the wind,” he says.

Ronan laughs. Leo points at the still tree. There is no wind at all.

On the second run, Leo beats Ronan. Ronan's shoe catches a little on the ground, but he does not fall. He wants to blame the shoe. He looks down at it. It still fits and the lace is tight.

“You got that one,” he says.

“One each,” Leo says.

They are about to start a third race. But the teacher calls them back. Ronan wants the last run. He wants to leave with two wins. But his legs are tired, and everyone is going inside.

At home, he tells Mum about the first race. He shows her the last two steps between the chair and the door.

“Did Leo finish too?” she asks.

“Right beside me.”

“And Jun?”

“Behind someone else. Because of the wind.”

Mum looks at the quiet curtains. Ronan explains the joke. She smiles and moves his cup away from the edge. Then he shows the steps again.

Later, Dad asks about the second race. Ronan tells him that part too. Then Dad says he will race Ronan to the kitchen.

Ronan stands up at once. Dad is already there. He holds out three bowls. “I win,” he says. He did not run at all.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

race＝赛跑；finish＝终点；breath＝呼吸。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan怎样在跑步中取得一次真胜利？
2. Leo为什么没有因此成为坏对手？

## 读句子

**Jun / points / at Ronan.** Jun／指向／Ronan。
